title: Adaptive guardrail playbook for interdependent rollouts (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, operational playbook for rolling out features that are interdependent (multiple services, multi-model routing, or hybrid hosted/dedicated paths). Focus is on adaptive guardrails — heuristics and short-run automations that keep experiments safe while allowing progressive exposure and fast iteration.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product managers, release engineers, SRE oncall, experiment owners, solutions eng.
- Scope: A/B and canary exposures that cut across teams (model, runtime, console, billing). Not a full release handbook — complements existing deployment runbooks.

Overview (one-liner):
Build a small set of composable guardrail primitives (traffic controls, automated rollback triggers, quick-fallback routes) plus a minimal telemetry contract so cross-team rollouts can be orchestrated with low cognitive load.

Core primitives (short):
- Exposure slices: microcohorts (geography, account-level, percent-sample). Keep slice metadata immutable once assigned.
- Safety fences: latency ceiling, error-rate delta, quality-regression signal (prompt-set evals), cost-surge threshold.
- Fast-fallback routes: model-variant fallback, region fallback, default-to-previous-version. Must be idempotent and safe to run automatically.
- Escalation gates: auto-pause + paging to oncall if two or more fences trip within 5 minutes.
- Visibility contract: per-slice dashboards updated every 30s for latency and 1m for quality drift.

Telemetry contract (minimal fields every team must emit):
- request_id, slice_id, exposure_bucket, model_version, backend_path (hosted/dedicated/private), latency_ms, token_count, error_type, response_quality_score (0-1), cost_estimate_usd.
Notes: quality_score can be synthetic (heuristic) for fast signal but must be correlated to eval-set metrics for decisioning.

Stakeholder lattice (operational mapping):
- Release owner (product): defines hypothesis + success metrics.
- Model owner (applied ml): provides baseline evals, known failure modes.
- Serving/runtime (infra): provides route config and fallback wiring.
- SRE: oncall escalation and incident playbook.
- Billing/finance contact: monitors cost surges for Dedicated reservations.
Each slice must have an assigned owner from each role. Put owners in the release charter.

Example flow (quick):
1) Dry-run in internal staging with synthetic traffic.
2) 0.1% canary to internal beta cohort (slice_id=beta-1). Observe 1h.
3) If no fence trips, escalate to 1% public microcohort split across regions.
4) After 6h stable, run short quality eval on production prompts (10k samples) and check model delta < 0.02.
5) Ramp to 10% with cost throttle enabled.
6) Full rollout after 48h stable and signoff.

Adaptive decision heuristics (examples to encode in console automation):
- Latency spike detection: if median latency increases >30% AND p95 > latency_SLO for two consecutive 5m windows => pause ramp and route traffic to fallback for 10 minutes, page SRE if auto-resolve fails.
- Quality drift: if response_quality_score delta vs baseline > 0.05 for two consecutive 1h windows => trigger canary hold and run full eval set.
- Cost runaway: if cost_estimate_usd per 1k requests > 2x baseline for sustained 30m => throttle tail traffic down to preserve budget and notify finance.

Runbook snippets (operational play):
- On auto-pause: owner gets notif in console, can click "inspect slice" (pre-populated query links), options: resume (requires human signoff), rollback to previous model, switch to fallback path.
- Emergency rollback: 1-click rollback in console that also clears ongoing queued requests to affected model pool. Must log reason and Jira ticket stub created automatically.

Observation checklist (pre-deploy):
- Are telemetry fields present and validated on staging? (smoketest query provided)
- Do fallback routes exist and have capacity? (capacity smoke test)
- Owners assigned for each slice and oncall rotation known?
- Cost guardrails configured (per-minute throttle)?
- Hypothesis and primary metric declared in release charter?

Templates and quick queries (to paste into console):
- Smoke latency: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, [50,95,99]) FROM requests WHERE slice_id = '{slice}' SINCE 10m
- Error spike: SELECT count(*) FILTER (error_type IS NOT NULL) / count(*) FROM requests WHERE slice_id = '{slice}' SINCE 5m
- Quality drift (heuristic): SELECT avg(response_quality_score) FROM requests WHERE slice_id = '{slice}' SINCE 1h COMPARE TO baseline

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to discuss):
- How strict should automated rollback be? (fast safety vs false positives causing churn)
- Should cost thresholds be soft (notify) or hard (automated throttle)?
- Where to store slice ownership metadata so it’s queryable by automation (convention vs single source of truth)?
- How to handle multi-model A/B where different models have different cold-start KV/cache behavior (affects latency heuristics)?

Implementation worklist (next 90 days):
- 2-week spike: add slice_id to all request headers + validation pipeline (infra).
- 3-week: build small console UI for guardrail config + one-click fallback (product/console).
- 6-week: add quality_score synthetic signal in serving runtime (applied-ml + infra).
- 10-week: automation for auto-pause with audit log and Jira stub (sre + release eng).

Quick notes / rough ideas (brainstorm-y):
- Consider a "safety index" computed from normalized signals (latency, error, quality, cost) to make multi-signal decisions simpler.
- Add a playground mode that replays production slices against new model in a shadow path for quick regression probing.
- Keep canary duration small for high-risk features (e.g., routing changes) but longer for content-quality features.

Contacts and availability:
- Aisha Patel (doc owner) — aisha@redwood.ai — core hours 9-5 PT.
- Miguel Hernandez (release eng) — slack: @miguelh — for console automations.

Notes to self (TODO):

- Draft console copy for auto-pause dialog (UX).
- Wire a demo for the next cross-functional cadence meeting.

End of doc (WIP).
